prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a city Solomon built, or the homeland of one of his wives or royal allies (not Sheba)
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a city Solomon built or fortified, or the homeland of one of his wives or royal allies (Kings and Chronicles; not the queen of Sheba). Trade lands of disputed site, such as Ophir and Tarshish, are not asked.
prompts.note: Jerusalem is scored as Israel, as in the other Bible prompts; Beth-horon the nether is in the West Bank.
prompts.summary: Solomon fortified Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer, built Tadmor and store cities in Hamath, and traded cedar with Hiram of Tyre. He married Pharaoh's daughter and many foreign wives from Moab, Ammon, Edom, Zidon and the Hittites (1 Kgs 3-11; 2 Chr 8-9).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Solomon built Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer (1 Kgs 9:15) and the temple at Jerusalem.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: He married Pharaoh's daughter, who brought Gezer as a dowry (1 Kgs 3:1; 9:16).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Hiram king of Tyre sent cedars of Lebanon for the temple, and Solomon loved women of the Zidonians (1 Kgs 5:1-10; 11:1).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: He loved women of the Moabites, Ammonites and Edomites (1 Kgs 11:1); Naamah the Ammonitess bore Rehoboam (1 Kgs 14:21).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: He built Tadmor in the wilderness and store cities in Hamath (2 Chr 8:3-4).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: He built Beth-horon the nether, now in the West Bank (1 Kgs 9:17).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: He loved Hittite women (1 Kgs 11:1); the Bible Dictionary says the Hittite empire reached into Asia Minor.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a place named in the Gospel of Matthew
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a land, city or region named in the Gospel of Matthew
prompts.note: Bethlehem and Jericho are in the West Bank (PSE); players may pin ISR, which is also correct for Jerusalem and Galilee.
prompts.summary: Matthew ranges well beyond Galilee. The infant Jesus was carried from Bethlehem to Egypt, his fame spread through Syria and Decapolis, and he went to the coasts of Tyre and Sidon and beyond the Jordan. Jesus cited the men of Nineveh, and Simon of Cyrene, from today's Libya, carried his cross.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Jerusalem, Nazareth and Galilee run through the whole Gospel (Matthew 2:1, 22-23).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Joseph took the young child and Mary into Egypt until Herod died (Matthew 2:14-15).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea and passed through Jericho (Matthew 2:1; 20:29).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Jesus departed into the coasts of Tyre and Sidon (Matthew 15:21).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: His fame went throughout all Syria, and crowds came from Decapolis (Matthew 4:24-25).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Jesus named the men of Nineveh, and the genealogy names the carrying away to Babylon (Matthew 12:41; 1:11).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Jesus came into the coasts of Judea beyond Jordan, east of the river (Matthew 19:1).

answers.name: Libya
answers.fact: Simon, who carried the cross, was a man of Cyrene, in eastern Libya (Matthew 27:32).

prompts.display_text: Pin a European country where the first Latter-day Saint converts were baptized between 1849 and 1851.
prompts.text_original: Between 1849 and 1851, apostles and other missionaries sent from Utah and Britain baptized the first Latter-day Saint converts in several European countries. Pin a country where, according to the Church Global Histories, the first converts were baptized in those years.
prompts.note: The Netherlands (1861), Belgium (1888) and Austria (1883) had their first baptisms later, so they do not count.
prompts.summary: Within three years of reaching the Salt Lake Valley, the Church sent apostles to open Europe beyond Britain. Erastus Snow led the Scandinavian work from Copenhagen, Lorenzo Snow opened Italy and Switzerland, and John Taylor went to France. Between 1849 and 1851 the first converts were baptized from Le Havre to Copenhagen, Schleswig and the Westman Islands.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: Fifteen people, including Ole and Marie Monster, became the first converts baptized in Denmark, August 12, 1850.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: Augustus Saint d'Anna, the first known convert in France, was baptized at Le Havre on July 30, 1849.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: George P. Dykes baptized Anna Hoth and her daughter Oline at Schleswig, September 15, 1851, the first recorded baptisms in present-day Germany.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Jean Antoine Bosc was baptized by Lorenzo Snow on October 27, 1850, the first convert baptized in Italy.

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: John E. Forsgren baptized 21 converts in Gavle and Stockholm, June-September 1850.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: The first converts in Switzerland were baptized in Geneva in March 1851.

answers.name: Norway
answers.fact: Hans F. Petersen baptized John Olsen and Peter Adamsen at Risor, November 26, 1851, the first baptisms in Norway.

answers.name: Iceland
answers.fact: Benedikt Hansson and Ragnhildur Stefansdottir became the first converts baptized in Iceland, May 1851.
